DIVISION OF EXISTENCE · FORM N-1 · ISSUED UNDER THE ELEMENTS, BOOK I, POSTULATES 1–5
This is to certify that the property known as
comprising eighteen rooms joined by twenty-two doorways, has been inspected room by room and found sound in every room; and that
the said property has been proved, by a method any reader may repeat, not to exist.
The property has passed every inspection except existence.
Four flights, each climbing one storey, arrive on the landing where the first began.
Carried once round, a frame of reference comes home changed: a rise of
thirty-eight feet eight inches, where any closed walk must rise not at all.
Five galleries, each turning right, enclose a single square court.
walk: C1 · C2 · C3 · C4 · C5
Carried once round, a frame of reference comes home changed: a turn of
four hundred and fifty degrees, where any closed walk must turn three
The hall measures a quarter inch longer than the rooms that run beside it.
walk: D03 · D02 · D01 · D05 · HALL
Carried once round, a frame of reference comes home changed: a gap of one
quarter of an inch, where any closed walk must close exactly.
closed walk would then come home unchanged: the product of the walk’s transformations would be the identity. Each of the three walks above comes home changed. Hence no such placement exists. ∎

Of the 1,540 ways of bricking up three doorways, exactly 64 would allow the property to exist; no single doorway, and no pair, suffices. The solver’s proof is printed in full around the border of this certificate.
